name: Hearing Buddy - Speech To Text
oneLine: An iPhone and iPad captioning app made by someone with hearing loss: free, unlimited captions that run on the phone, captions shared with phones nearby, and Apple Watch name alerts with Buddy+.

platforms.text: iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch; Mac and Vision Pro with Buddy+
platforms.detail: Apple devices only: there is no Android version and no web app. Live captions on Mac and Apple Vision Pro are part of Buddy+. A search of Google Play finds no Hearing Buddy app.

deviceRequirements.detail: iPhone and iPad need iOS 26 or later, and Apple Watch features watchOS 10 or later. Buddy's Notes (summaries) need iOS 27 on an iPhone with Apple Intelligence. Hearing Buddy calls the iOS 26 requirement its biggest weakness.

roomCaptions.detail: Speech picked up by the microphone becomes text as people speak, with no minute meter and no session cap. It does not caption audio from other apps.

groupConversations.text: Share Captions: nearby iPhones and iPads
groupConversations.detail: One phone captions the room and others read along on their own iPhone or iPad; more people can turn on their microphone and every voice goes into one transcript. Devices connect directly, with no internet, account or server. Free, same room only, and every reader needs the app on iOS 26.

languages.detail: English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin and Cantonese, in 18 language and regional options. Captions can be translated into 10 reading languages.

offline.text: Yes, captions run on the phone
offline.detail: On-device captions work with no signal. Translation works offline after a one-time download of each language. Enhanced Accuracy, an optional mode you turn on, makes captions in the cloud.

speakerLabels.text: By name per phone; Buddy+ colours for 4 voices
speakerLabels.detail: In shared sessions each person's words appear by name in their own colour. On one phone, Hearing Buddy's own comparison (July 2026) and educator pages describe Speaker Labels in Buddy+: colours for up to four voices, reset after each session. The App Store listing does not list Speaker Labels.

voiceNames.text: No, labels reset after each session
voiceNames.detail: Buddy+ Speaker Labels tell up to four voices apart by colour without training anyone's voice, and reset when the session ends.

translation.text: Live, on the phone, 10 languages; Buddy+ alone
translation.detail: Captions are translated on the phone into English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, or Simplified or Traditional Chinese, offline after a one-time download. Free for everyone in a shared session; translating your own captions alone needs Buddy+. Cantonese can't be translated.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, text on the phone, free
saveTranscripts.detail: Every session is saved on your phone automatically. Nothing is uploaded and there is no account; a deleted transcript is gone.

export.text: Copy and share; formats not stated
export.detail: You can copy and share transcripts for free; the file formats are not stated. The Mac companion app saves transcripts as text files.

fileUpload.detail: Hearing Buddy's pages describe live captions from the microphone, not transcribing audio or video files.

summaries.detail: Conversation summaries are part of Buddy+. Buddy's Notes, written when you finish, need iOS 27 on an iPhone with Apple Intelligence. Apple's award page says the summaries are made with Apple's on-device frameworks.

customWords.detail: The App Store notes mention a Cloud Enhanced dictionary for adding words, and the privacy policy says your name and word list help Enhanced Accuracy spell them right. A word list for the on-device captions is not described.

display.detail: Text size is adjustable for free, and the listing says text can go to 200% or more. The app supports VoiceOver, Reduce Motion and a dark interface.

soundAlerts.detail: Hearing Buddy alerts you when someone says your name or asks you a question (Buddy+). Its pages don't describe alerts for sounds like a doorbell or an alarm.

phoneCalls.detail: It can't caption phone or FaceTime calls on iPhone, because iOS doesn't let microphone apps reach call audio. Hearing Buddy points to Apple's Live Captions and FCC-funded relay services instead.

videoCalls.text: Not on iPhone; on Mac with Buddy+
videoCalls.detail: On iPhone it can't caption FaceTime or other apps. The privacy policy (October 2026) says Hearing Buddy for Mac can caption speech playing on the Mac, such as calls and videos; Mac captions are part of Buddy+.

mediaOnDevice.detail: Videos, podcasts and voice notes playing on the phone can't be captioned. On a Mac, the privacy policy describes captioning Mac audio.

humanCaptioners.detail: Hearing Buddy offers no human-reviewed captions and says that for ADA-grade access you want a human captioner or a certified service.

signLanguage.detail: Hearing Buddy's pages don't describe sign language features.

privacy.text: On the phone; optional cloud mode
privacy.detail: By default speech recognition runs on the device and audio and transcripts are not collected. Enhanced Accuracy, off until you turn it on, streams audio to a cloud speech-recognition provider; the privacy policy says neither Hearing Buddy nor the provider stores the audio or captions. Shared captions go directly between nearby devices.

account.detail: Captions work the first time you open the app, with no sign-up and no credit card.

availability.text: App Store: US, UK, Germany, Japan, India and more
availability.detail: Opened on the App Store in the US, UK, Germany, Japan and India (October 2026); Hearing Buddy publishes no country list. The app's own menus are in 8 languages. Not on Google Play.

freePlan.detail: Free with no account or card: unlimited live captions, Share Captions, translation inside shared sessions, background listening, saved transcripts, copy and share, and text size. The cloud Enhanced Accuracy mode has 30 free minutes.

price.detail: Buddy+ on the US App Store listing, October 2026, with 20 hours a month of Enhanced Accuracy (240 a year on Annual) and hour packs for more. Hearing Buddy's website lists lower prices: US$9.99 a month, US$59.99 a year or US$7.99 a week, and a 14-day free trial. The website also sells Buddy+ Lifetime (no price shown).

accessibilityFunding.detail: No government programme is described; the live captions themselves are free. Educators can ask for free Buddy+ on their own device.

strengths.text: Live captions are free and unlimited, run on the phone, and work without internet.
Share Captions lets nearby iPhones and iPads read the same captions, each in their own language, free and with no internet or account.
With Buddy+, an Apple Watch taps your wrist when someone says your name or asks you a question.
Apple named it a finalist in the Inclusivity category of the 2026 Apple Design Awards.

limits.text: Needs iOS 26 or later and runs only on Apple devices; there is no Android version or web app.
Live captions cover 8 languages, and translation 10 reading languages.
Shared captions only work between devices in the same room, and every reader needs the app on iOS 26.
Translation on your own, summaries, name alerts, Boost Audio and Mac captions need Buddy+.

sources.title: Features — What Hearing Buddy Does
quotes: Speech becomes clear text as it is spoken, with no minute meter and no session cap. Processed on your phone, so it works with no signal at all.

Unlimited live captions, Share Captions, translation for everyone inside a shared session, background listening, saved transcripts, copy and share, and text size. Those are not a trial — they stay free.
Buddy+ adds Boost Audio, Watch alerts, summaries, solo translation, and Mac and Vision Pro support for $59.99 a year, $9.99 a month, or $7.99 a week.
Our biggest real weakness. If you're setting up a phone for a parent on an older iPhone, Hearing Buddy may not install at all — and other captioning apps run on much older versions.
iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro. There is no Android version and no web app, so a mixed-device group will leave someone out.
Does my audio go to a cloud service? No. Speech recognition and translation run on your device, and shared sessions pass captions directly between the phones in the room rather than through a server.
No. iOS does not let microphone apps reach call audio, so no app in this category can.
For ADA-grade access at a legal proceeding or a public event, you want a human captioner or a certified service — not an app on a table.

sources.title: Live Translation — Read Conversations in Your Language
quotes: It is built on Apple's on-device translation, which means the text is processed on your phone rather than sent to a translation service.
When you are captioning solo, translation is part of Buddy+.
After that, translation runs entirely offline.
English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.

sources.title: Boost Audio — Turn Your Headphones Into a Sound Amplifier
quotes: Boost Audio turns AirPods, Bluetooth, or wired headphones into a real-time sound amplifier — lifting speech by up to 39 dB and shaping it to your own hearing test from Apple Health.
It is not a hearing aid

sources.title: Privacy Policy - Hearing Buddy
quotes: Last updated: October 22, 2026

Speech recognition and language processing happen on your device by default. We do not collect or store your audio or transcripts. The one exception is the optional Enhanced Accuracy feature, described below, which streams audio to a cloud caption service only while you have it turned on.
Neither we nor the provider store the audio or the captions; our server records only the number of seconds streamed so it can meter your included hours.
Hearing Buddy for Mac captions what your microphone hears and, if you choose Mac Audio, speech playing on your Mac, such as calls and videos.
Your name and word list go along to help spell them right.
Captions you choose to share go directly to devices near you over your local network. No server is involved.

notes: Conflicts: (1) Price: the US App Store listing (version 3.19, 28 Oct 2026) says 'Buddy+ Annual: $89.99 per year' and 'Buddy+ Monthly: $14.99 per month'; the website's features, real-time transcription and Boost Audio pages say $59.99/year, $9.99/month or $7.99/week, and its comparison and educator pages say $59.99/year. The US App Store In-App Purchases list shows Pro $89.99, $79.99, $59.99, $14.99, $6.99, $9.99, Buddy+ Annual $99.99 and $79.99, Pro $59.99 and $9.99 (periods not named). The table uses the listing's description prices. (2) Cloud: the homepage says '100% on device, private, no cloud' and the features FAQ answers 'Does my audio go to a cloud service? No.', while the App Store listing and the privacy policy (22 Oct 2026) describe the optional Enhanced Accuracy mode that streams audio to a cloud speech-recognition provider (named as Meta in the policy). (3) Speaker Labels: listed as a Buddy+ feature on Hearing Buddy's Ava comparison (1 Jul 2026), Live Transcribe comparison (6 Jul 2026) and educator page, but not in the current App Store or features-page Buddy+ lists; llms.txt says 'speaker identification'. (4) Mac: the Mac App Store app 'Hearing Buddy Everywhere' (version 2.21, May 2026, macOS 14.6+) is a companion display that needs the iPhone app with Buddy+; the privacy policy describes a Mac app that captions the microphone and Mac audio and writes notes with Apple Private Cloud Compute; the iOS app's listing also lists Mac (macOS 26, M1 or later). Which Mac app is current is unclear. (5) Trial: Hearing Buddy's roundup (6 Oct 2026) says Buddy+ has a 14-day free trial and the App Store notes (3.15, 3.08) mention Buddy+ trials; the App Store description only mentions 30 free minutes of Enhanced Accuracy. (6) Names: the US listing is 'Hearing Buddy - Speech To Text', Apple's award page links it as 'hearing-buddy-live-captions', the German listing is 'Hearing Buddy: Live-Untertitel' (same app id 6747363502). Apple's award page names the developer as Lilly Seay; the App Store seller is Krager Labs LLC (Portland, Oregon, per the terms). (7) The App Store privacy label lists Identifiers under 'Data Used to Track You' and Device ID for third-party advertising (not linked to you); the website uses a Meta Pixel on its Buddy+ quiz pages only. Not shown on the page. Awards: the 2026 Apple Design Award finalist (Inclusivity) is confirmed on developer.apple.com/design/awards (the category winner was Guitar Wiz). The App Store page also shows Editors' Choice and an 'Apps We Love' story; not used. Not found / not opened: there is no help centre (help.hearingbuddyapp.com does not resolve; /faq, /help and /pricing return 404), so FAQs come from the feature pages. Google Play search finds no Hearing Buddy app (an unrelated Android app called 'AI Caption Buddy' exists). Web search was unavailable during research, so press coverage was not checked. Availability: the app opened on the App Store in the US, UK, Germany, Japan and India, and the lookup API also returned it for Slovenia, Australia, Canada and Brazil. The website's browser speech-to-text tool (a few free cloud minutes) is not counted as a web app; Hearing Buddy itself says there is no web app. Caption accuracy was not checked. All pages opened 2026-10-28 with curl.
